attribution: Prices are from PriceCharting (https://www.pricecharting.com/). Every entry's `url` is the PriceCharting product page it was read from - link back to it when you show these prices.
method: Read from PriceCharting's public set listing pages (one page per set, 35 pages, plus its Pokemon Promo page for SWSH/SVP promos), loaded one at a time in a normal browser session; the page's own 'load more rows' requests were used for long sets, paced about 2 seconds apart. The visible Ungraded / Grade 9 / PSA 10 price columns were copied as shown (checksum-verified, no retyping) and matched to this mirror's card ids by set + collector number + name. Not an API or bulk download, no PriceCharting account or subscription, and not on an automated refresh schedule (unlike data/sets/ and data/psa/) - re-run manually when it goes stale. The 124 cards added on 2026-09-07 were looked up individually, one product page at a time; any of those that fall in the sets above (the 16 Scarlet & Violet Energy cards) were refreshed by this pass; the other 108 keep their own `readOn` date (2026-09-07) on the entry instead of the file-level `pricesReadOn`.
coverage: Every Scarlet & Violet-era set in the mirror (Scarlet & Violet through Destined Rivals, Black Bolt, White Flare, SVE energies, SVP promos) and every Sword & Shield-era set (Sword & Shield through Crown Zenith, including Celebrations, Pokemon GO, Trainer Gallery / Galarian Gallery / Shiny Vault subsets and SWSH promos). Mega Evolution-era sets and older eras are not covered yet, except the 108 individually looked up cards.
note: Grade 9 and PSA 10 are PriceCharting's own price points and for rarely-traded cards they can rest on a few sales, so large jumps between ungraded, grade9 and psa10 (e.g. a $0.25 card with a $325 grade9) are often thin-sample noise, not market consensus. Only the plain card is recorded for each id: PriceCharting's reverse-holo / Poke Ball / Master Ball / stamped / prize-pack / jumbo variants are not included. Two older entries (McDonald's 2018 Pikachu #4 and Chansey #10) have similar anomalies.
